newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court postpones ruling on pay claim.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court postpones ruling on pay claim.

text.p: Brazil's highest court Wednesday postponed a ruling on a controversial 28.9 percent public sector claim for a pay raise, a spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman for the Supreme Federal Tribunal said there was no specific reason for the delay and that a judgement was now expected on February 19.

The case was brought by 11 civil servants who claim they are entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise given to the armed forces in 1993. The workers say federal rules state pay rises for one category must apply for all.

Government officials, fearing the impact such a large raise would have on already-pressured public finances, fear a ruling in favour of the group would set a precedent for the rest of the public sector, which has not seen a wage increase for two years.
Newspapers report that an across-the-board 28.9 percent increase would hike federal payroll costs by $7.0 billion. In 1996, the government spent $42 billion on payroll.
